key_insight: Photon-drag photocurrents in altermagnets split into symmetry-distinct angular harmonics that encode both the magnetic order and the Néel domain, enabling all-optical domain readout.
engineering_relevance: This provides a symmetry-based route to noncontact magnetic sensing and domain discrimination in optoelectronic devices, especially where conventional bulk photovoltaic readout is forbidden.
method: Analyze second-order photocurrents driven by finite photon momentum in altermagnetic crystals.
Decompose the response into angular harmonics and compare domain-even vs domain-odd components under 90° sample rotation.
Track how linear versus circular polarization changes which microscopic current channels carry the domain-odd signal.
evidence_signal: From the abstract’s symmetry analysis, tetragonal d-wave altermagnets place domain-even and domain-odd currents in different harmonics, while mirror symmetries and polarization determine which microscopic terms contribute to each channel.
watch_item: The domain-odd charge current requires spin-orbit coupling to be observable, so materials with weak SOC may give a much smaller experimental signal.
paper_title: Reading Altermagnetic Domains with Photon Drag
